stories.title: M S Dhoni retires from playing in the IPL and becomes Chennai Super Kings' team mentor from 2027.
stories.summary: Chennai Super Kings said on 17 November that Dhoni, 45, has ended his IPL playing career after 278 matches and five titles and will be Team Mentor from IPL 2027 (Sky Sports, Indian Opinion).
stories.heat: Indian Opinion's source list shows 30+ outlets on it (The Hindu, Indian Express, Times of India, Business Standard, India Today, The National) plus Sky Sports abroad · two of the top four cards on the 17 November India digest · velocity: high, announced 17 November and tribute and records pieces still multiplying
detail: Mahendra Singh Dhoni has retired from playing in the Indian Premier League. Chennai Super Kings (CSK) announced on Tuesday 17 November 2026 that he will serve as the franchise's Team Mentor from the 2027 season, Sky Sports and Indian Opinion reported.

Sky Sports gives his IPL record as 5,439 runs at an average of 38.30 in 278 matches. Indian Opinion, summarising Aaj Tak and TV9 Hindi, adds 264 sixes and 158 catches. He led CSK to five titles. CSK bought him at the first auction in 2008, and he spent 17 of his 19 seasons there, with two at Rising Pune Supergiant while CSK were suspended (Sky Sports).

He did not play in the most recent season: Sky Sports says a calf strain kept him out of all of it, which in effect ended his playing career. Organiser says his last IPL appearance was in 2025 against Gujarat Titans. OpIndia reports that CSK's management learned of his decision only on Tuesday.

CSK owner N Srinivasan said on the club's website: "There is no CSK without MS Dhoni." Managing director K S Viswanathan said the club will miss seeing him in yellow on the field but is glad he will keep guiding the players (Sky Sports). Indian Opinion reports that Dhoni posted an Instagram reel set to the song it names as "Main Har Ik Pal Ka Shayar Hoon", which it says he also used when he left international cricket in August 2020.

Dhoni retired from international cricket in 2020 after leading India to World Cup titles in both the T20 and 50-over formats. The timing matters for CSK's squad planning: Indian Opinion's source list includes Hindustan Times and India Today pieces on how his exit changes the franchise's retentions and auction budget for 2027.

stories.title: India beat Pakistan 2-1 in the SAFF Championship final in Dhaka to win a record 10th title.
stories.summary: India came from a goal down against a ten-man Pakistan on 17 November, with Sandip Mandi heading the winner in the 88th minute (Nukta, Pakistan Today); Pakistan's players then gave India a guard of honour, according to Sportstar as summarised by Indian Opinion.
stories.heat: two cards in the top four of the 18 November India digest · carried in India (Sportstar, Mathrubhumi, Asianet) and Pakistan (Nukta, Pakistan Today) · velocity: high, played on the evening of 17 November, guard of honour clip driving a second wave
detail: India won the 2026 SAFF Championship by beating Pakistan 2-1 at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Tuesday 17 November. It is India's 10th title in the South Asian tournament, a record, and Indian Opinion's digest calls it the third in a row.

Pakistan led at half-time. Alamgir Ghazi scored in first-half stoppage time, curling the ball into the far corner from a Junaid Shah cross (Nukta). The match turned around the hour mark, when Junaid Shah was sent off for a dangerous challenge on Brison Fernandes: the referee first gave only a free kick, and a VAR review changed it to a straight red card. Nukta times the red card at 61 minutes, Indian Opinion at 58.

Suhail Ahmad Bhat equalised for India shortly afterwards. Nukta says it was his fourth goal of the tournament, which made him its top scorer. Sandip Mandi won it in the 88th minute with a header from an Abdul Rabeeh corner that went in off the post.

After the final whistle Pakistan's players and coach formed a guard of honour for the Indian team, Indian Opinion reports, citing Sportstar (The Hindu). The gesture drew attention because sporting ties between the two countries have been strained since the 2025 Pahalgam attack; India's coach Naushad Moosa had said before the tournament that his team would take part in pre-match greetings.

It was Pakistan's first SAFF final. The team, coached by Nolberto Solano, had beaten the Maldives 3-0 and knocked out hosts Bangladesh in the semi-final (Nukta). Mathrubhumi, via Indian Opinion, puts India's record against Pakistan at 18 wins in 31 meetings.

stories.title: The Earthshot Prize was awarded in India for the first time, in Mumbai, and an Indian electric rickshaw maker was one of the five winners.
stories.summary: At the 17 November ceremony attended by the Prince and Princess of Wales, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility won the Clean Our Air prize of £1 million; the couple are due to meet Prime Minister Modi on 18 November (BBC report carried by Yahoo News).
stories.heat: BBC via Yahoo, ABC News, NBC News, Gulf News, People · strong celebrity pull (Tendulkar, Alia Bhatt, Karan Johar) · velocity: high on 17 November, one more day of the visit to come
detail: New since the last edition, which covered the couple's arrival in Mumbai and the street cricket with Sachin Tendulkar on 16 November: the Earthshot Prize ceremony itself took place on Tuesday 17 November at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai. It was the sixth edition of Prince William's environmental prize and the first held in India. Five winners were chosen from 15 finalists and each receives £1 million to scale up (Yahoo News, carrying the BBC report).

The Indian winner was Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, in the Clean Our Air category, for a plan to roll out up to one million electric rickshaws. Earlier in the day the couple rode one of its electric rickshaws to meet the finalists; William called it "quite good fun, really good fun".

The other winners: Bhutan (Protect and Restore Nature), for policies that protect water supplies for nearly a fifth of the world's population; PFAS-Free France (Build a Waste-Free World), a campaign behind a French law banning "forever chemicals" by 2030; the Niue Ocean Wide Trust from the Pacific island of Niue (Revive Our Oceans); and the energy company Ørsted (Fix Our Climate), which has cut its direct carbon emissions by more than 98%.

Karan Johar hosted. Guests included Sachin Tendulkar, Alia Bhatt, Sonam Kapoor and Rami Malek, and Shreya Ghoshal and Take That were among the performers (Yahoo News, Gulf News). Catherine presented one of the awards. William wore a bandhgala and Catherine an anarkali by the designer Mahima Mahajan.
The visit ends on Wednesday 18 November, when the couple are expected to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It is their first official overseas trip together in four years.
stories.about: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility is the Mahindra group's unit for small electric three-wheelers and four-wheelers used for short-distance passenger and goods transport.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan is now forecast to hit the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Tuni around noon on 20 November, and evacuations have begun.
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department expects Akvan to strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm with winds of 120 to 130 km/h and gusts to 145 km/h (Indian Opinion citing TV9 Hindi); The Week reports thousands already evacuated, and Odisha is deploying 60 state and 14 national disaster response teams.
stories.heat: The Week, Business Standard, The Hans India, Daily Jagran live tracker, TV9 Hindi · velocity: high and rising, landfall still two days away
detail: New since the last edition's cyclone watch: the storm now has a forecast landfall. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) expects Cyclone Akvan to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Tuni on Friday 20 November, around noon according to tracker summaries of the IMD forecast. No landfall, damage or deaths from Akvan had been reported as of the morning of 18 November.

The IMD forecast, as reported by Indian Opinion from TV9 Hindi, is for sustained winds of 120 to 130 km/h with gusts up to 145 km/h. The system was expected to become a severe cyclonic storm by the evening of 17 November and a very severe cyclonic storm by 19 November. Heavy to very heavy rain is forecast from 17 to 21 November across Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Telangana, and further inland.

The Week's report of 17 November is headlined with thousands evacuated; a search summary of the day's coverage puts the number moved at over 80,000, a figure this edition could not tie to a named official. Fishermen have been told not to go to sea until 20 November. Reports differ on the alert colour for Andhra Pradesh: The Hans India says orange, another report says yellow.

Odisha has put Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts on alert and plans to deploy 60 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force teams and 14 National Disaster Response Force teams. The IMD says a direct hit on Odisha is unlikely, but heavy rain is expected there from 18 November (Indian Opinion).

Akvan is the third cyclone to threaten the east coast in about three weeks. Arnab struck Andhra Pradesh on 28 October and Murasu on 2 to 3 November. Estimates of the combined loss vary: Indian Opinion gives the state's initial estimate as about Rs 5,000 crore with more than 3.6 lakh hectares of crops affected, and The Week's coverage cites nearly Rs 7,000 crore.

stories.title: Bilkis Bano says she is in shock after the Supreme Court suspended the life sentences of two men convicted in her gang-rape case and gave them bail without hearing her.
stories.summary: The order of 28 October by Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale became public on 16 November (Bar and Bench); Bano said on 17 November she learned of it from press reports and will challenge it (The Tribune, The Wire).
stories.heat: Bar and Bench, LiveLaw, The News Minute, India TV, The Tribune, The Wire, Telangana Today, DT Next · trending topic on X · velocity: high, order surfaced 16 November, her statement 17 November, challenge promised
detail: The Supreme Court has suspended the life sentences of two convicts in the Bilkis Bano gang-rape and murder case and granted them bail while their appeals are pending. Bar and Bench reported the order on 16 November. Search summaries of The News Minute and the rights group CJP date the order to 28 October and name the bench as Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale, and the two men as Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Mordhiya.

The bench cited the fact that the men have been in prison for more than seventeen years and that one of them is severely handicapped (Bar and Bench). The order came on their appeals against the Bombay High Court's 2017 judgment, which upheld their conviction and sentence. The court said there are issues of fact and law to be decided in the appeal.

Bano responded on 17 November. She said she was in "pain, shock and disbelief" (The Wire) and that she found out from press reports. "This is the second time an order has been passed without calling or hearing me," she said, according to The Tribune, which also reports that she intends to challenge the bail and feels she is "losing the justice I fought for". LiveLaw's Supreme Court round-up for 17 November also records that she says she was not heard.

Background: Bano was gang-raped and members of her family were killed during the 2002 Gujarat riots. Eleven men were sentenced to life. Gujarat released all eleven on remission in 2022; the Supreme Court struck that down on 8 January 2024 and ordered them back to prison. The two men given bail now are among those eleven. CJP's analysis notes that the new order does not address the court's earlier dismissal of the convicts' petitions against the 2017 High Court judgment.

stories.title: Modi ended his Manila visit with a list of offers to ASEAN, including free e-visas for its tourists and a maritime cooperation plan, and attended a Quad leaders' meeting.
stories.summary: At the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit on 17 November, Modi called for "peace, stability and predictability" and announced maritime, cyber, nuclear and space initiatives with ASEAN; he returned to Delhi early on 18 November (Asianet Newsable citing ANI, Indian Opinion).
stories.heat: ANI, The Tribune, India TV, Open, Asianet; 5 sources on the Indian Opinion card · velocity: medium, visit closed in the early hours of 18 November
detail: New since the last edition, which had Modi arriving in Manila: on Tuesday 17 November he addressed the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit, joined a Quad leaders' meeting on the sidelines, and flew back to New Delhi in the early hours of Wednesday (Asianet Newsable, citing ANI). This card covers only the India side; the summit as a whole is on the world board.

Indian Opinion, summarising five outlets, reports that Modi said the world needs peace, stability and predictability after a run of crises since the Covid-19 pandemic. He named terrorism, cyber fraud, online scams and attacks on seafarers as shared threats and repeated India's support for a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific. The reference to seafarers came a day after a missile hit an LPG tanker with 24 Indian crew near the Strait of Hormuz (that attack is on the war board).

His announcements to ASEAN, as listed by Asianet Newsable: a long-term ASEAN-India Maritime Cooperation Plan (connectivity, coast guard cooperation, maritime domain awareness, seafarers' security), a joint cyber forensics training programme, technical exchanges on nuclear energy, a space hackathon, cooperation on mining and critical minerals, more scholarships for ASEAN students at Nalanda University, and free e-visas for tourists from ASEAN countries. The summit adopted an ASEAN-India Joint Statement on Cooperation in Disaster Management.

At the Quad meeting Modi sat with US President Donald Trump, Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and described the group as a constructive and trusted partnership, according to search summaries of India TV's coverage. The reports found give no India-specific outcome from the Quad meeting and nothing on any Modi and Trump exchange about the pending trade deal.

stories.title: India's envoy to Canada says the two countries are "on the cusp" of a free trade agreement, with Modi due in Canada on 11 and 12 December.
stories.summary: High Commissioner Dinesh Patnaik said on 17 November that a deal is close 16 years after talks began and that a defence agreement is likely to be signed on the trip (The Globe and Mail); ThePrint reports three services chapters are closed in a round that runs in New Delhi until 20 November.
stories.heat: Ground News: 28 sources, 75% left coverage · The Globe and Mail, ThePrint, Business Standard, Deccan Herald, BusinessToday · velocity: medium and rising towards the December visit
detail: Dinesh Patnaik, India's High Commissioner to Canada, said on Tuesday 17 November that India and Canada are "on the cusp" of finalising a free trade agreement, The Globe and Mail reported. Talks first began in 2010 and were shut down in 2023. Patnaik also said a defence agreement will likely be signed during Prime Minister Modi's visit, and that "fringe issues" should not derail progress.

Modi is expected in Toronto and Ottawa on 11 and 12 December, just before the G20 summit in Miami (The Globe and Mail). ThePrint says it would be his first standalone bilateral visit to Canada in more than a decade. Canada's trade minister Maninder Sidhu has said Canada wants to sign before the end of the year. Reports differ on whether December brings a signing or only an announcement that talks have concluded.

On the state of the talks, ThePrint reports that negotiators have closed three services chapters of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). The sixth round is under way in New Delhi from 11 to 20 November, five rounds were completed in seven months, and another is planned for December. The agreement spans 16 policy areas. Negotiators are also working on language to ease Canadian potash shipments to India.

The numbers: two-way trade in goods and services was C$30.4 billion in 2025 and Ottawa wants C$70 billion a year by 2030 (The Globe and Mail). India's goods exports to Canada were $2.67 billion in April to September 2026, up 18% on the year (ThePrint).

The thaw follows a rupture in 2023, when Ottawa accused Indian officials of a role in the killing of a Canadian Sikh activist in British Columbia, and both sides expelled diplomats in 2024. Prime Ministers Carney and Modi agreed to launch formal trade talks in November 2025, and Carney visited India in March 2026.

stories.title: Meta says it has changed Instagram's recommendation system in India to show less sexually suggestive and violent content.
stories.summary: Meta announced the change on 17 November, five weeks after India's technology ministry asked it to review how it ranks and recommends posts; it applies to recommendations from accounts a user does not follow and is not a ban (Reuters, carried by The Star).
stories.heat: Ground News: 19 sources · Reuters wire (The Star, TradingView), The Tribune, The Next Web, Digg · velocity: medium, one-day story with a regulatory tail
detail: Meta said on Tuesday 17 November that it has tuned Instagram's recommendation systems for India so that users see less "sexually suggestive" and violent material, Reuters reported. The change covers recommended posts from accounts a user does not follow. Meta said it affects what Instagram promotes and is not a blanket ban on such content.

The announcement follows an advisory of 10 October 2026 in which the technology ministry asked Meta to review its ranking and recommendation systems so that misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material is not amplified out of proportion, and to strengthen checks on content that could incite violence or disturb public order. A separate request asked Meta not to expose users disproportionately to a single or narrow set of narratives, and to report what it had done. Meta did not link its change to the advisory (Reuters).

Meta said users in India now flag recommended content about half as often as a year ago, according to search summaries of the Reuters report. It published no underlying figures, so the claim rests on Meta's word.

India is Instagram's largest market by users, and the government has been tightening its oversight of online content. Reuters notes that Meta has previously adjusted ranking on Facebook in countries including Canada and Brazil to reduce political content.

stories.title: Bangladesh's border guards detained an armed Indian BSF jawan who strayed about 200 yards across the border in Sylhet; one report says he has been returned.
stories.summary: Border Guard Bangladesh held the jawan on 17 November at Bichanakandi, where there is no fence, and a flag meeting was arranged (PTI via Deccan Herald and Indian Opinion); The Daily Jagran, citing ANI, says he came back safely after that meeting.
stories.heat: PTI wire, Deccan Herald, ETV Bharat, Hindustan Times, Daily Jagran, Bangladeshi media; videos circulating · velocity: medium, detained and reportedly released the same day
detail: Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) detained an armed jawan of India's Border Security Force (BSF) on Tuesday 17 November after he crossed about 200 yards into Bangladesh at Bichanakandi in Gowainghat, Sylhet district, opposite Meghalaya. The BGB put the crossing at around 12:30 pm local time. Lt Col Nur Uddin Ahmad, who commands the BGB's Sylhet Battalion, confirmed the detention (Indian Opinion, from PTI).

An Indian official told Hindustan Times that the jawan "inadvertently entered Bangladesh at the Bichnakandi border in Sylhet, where there is no fencing", The Daily Jagran reports. Reports say local residents surrounded him before BGB personnel took him away, and videos of this circulated; The Daily Jagran said it could not verify them.

A flag meeting between senior officers of the two forces was arranged to bring him back, officials told PTI. The Daily Jagran, citing ANI, reports that he returned safely to India after the meeting. The other reports found were written while the meeting was still pending, so the return rests on that one report.
The BSF guards the 4,096 km India-Bangladesh border, long stretches of which are unfenced. The incident passed without a confrontation between the two forces.

stories.title: The Sensex rose 427 points to 82,532 on 17 November, a second day of gains led by banks, while global technology shares fell.
stories.summary: The Sensex closed at 82,532.19 (up 0.52%) and the Nifty 50 at 25,387.40 (up 0.38%), with the Nifty Bank index touching a record intraday high of 62,414.90 (Business Standard, HDFC Sky, IIFL).
stories.heat: Business Standard, HDFC Sky, 5paisa, IIFL, Equentis · routine daily market coverage · velocity: medium, second day of a rally against a weak Wall Street
detail: New since the last edition's close of 82,104.79: on Tuesday 17 November the BSE Sensex gained 427.40 points, or 0.52%, to end at 82,532.19, and the NSE Nifty 50 gained 96.30 points, or 0.38%, to end at 25,387.40 (HDFC Sky; Business Standard's closing headline gives the same figures).

Banks led. The Nifty Bank index touched a record intraday high of 62,414.90 (IIFL, Equentis), the PSU bank index rose nearly 2%, and realty also gained. Mahindra & Mahindra, Axis Bank, Eicher Motors, Asian Paints and InterGlobe Aviation were the top Nifty gainers; HCL Technologies, Power Grid, Coal India, HDFC Life and Infosys lagged. The gains were narrow: more shares fell than rose (2,148 against 2,012), and the smallcap index slipped 0.22% (HDFC Sky).

The rise came against a sharp fall on Wall Street on Monday, when the Nasdaq lost 2.49% and the S&P 500 lost 1.92% on worries about AI valuations and tighter US curbs on China's access to advanced chips. HDFC Sky says foreign investors have put a record $9.53 billion into Indian equities so far in November, and Brent crude eased to about $91.70 a barrel.

On the currency, one market report in search results says the rupee gained about 0.5% to close at 93.47 to the dollar, its strongest in seven months. A second source for that figure was not found. No Reserve Bank of India announcement was found in the window.

stories.title: The Supreme Court will hear on 18 November a bar association plea for criminal contempt against a lawyer who told the Chief Justice he did not deserve his chair.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court Bar Association moved against advocate Pravin Singhal after his outburst in court on 16 November, with the Attorney General's consent (Hindustan Times and LiveLaw, via Indian Opinion); on 17 November the court also told Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut that apologies must come "from the heart".
stories.heat: Hindustan Times, LiveLaw, Times of India, New Indian Express, National Herald; 4 sources on the Indian Opinion card · velocity: medium, hearing listed for today
detail: The Supreme Court is due to hear on Wednesday 18 November a petition by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) seeking criminal contempt action against advocate Pravin Singhal. On Monday 16 November Singhal, pressing for an urgent hearing, told the bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant: "You can't sit in that chair, you don't deserve. You don't have the integrity for that!" Security escorted him out (Indian Opinion, summarising Hindustan Times and LiveLaw).

The Chief Justice agreed to list the matter after the SCBA obtained the consent of Attorney General R Venkataramani, which the Contempt of Courts Act requires. The SCBA called the conduct "extremely scandalous and unpardonable". Indian Opinion says it is the association's third contempt action over remarks about this Chief Justice.

Separately, on Tuesday 17 November, the court took up the contempt case against Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut over his remarks about the Chief Justice and the judiciary. It said a seasoned politician should show restraint and that apologies must come "from the heart", and directed Raut and journalist Nikhil Wagle to file affidavits on their social media posts. The next hearing is on 8 December (Times of India and New Indian Express, via Indian Opinion; LiveLaw's round-up of 17 November lists both matters).

stories.title: Stage III pollution curbs were lifted in Delhi-NCR on 17 November after the air quality index fell to 204.
stories.summary: The Commission for Air Quality Management revoked GRAP Stage III, in force since 6 November when the index reached 382, after three days of improvement; Stages I and II stay (Hindustan Times and Mint, via Indian Opinion).
stories.heat: Hindustan Times, Mint, TV9 Hindi, Times Now; 4 sources on the Indian Opinion card · velocity: low to medium, one-day administrative news
detail: The sub-committee of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) revoked Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across Delhi-NCR on Tuesday 17 November. Delhi's daily air quality index had fallen to 204, in the "poor" band, after three days of decline. Stage III had been imposed on 6 November, when the index hit 382, and brought a ban on most construction and demolition (Indian Opinion, summarising Hindustan Times, Mint and TV9 Hindi).

Stage I and Stage II measures remain in force. So do the CAQM's separate precautionary orders of 5 November, which limit dust-generating construction and require work from home for many offices; those run until 20 November and will be reviewed after that. Mint reports that of Delhi's monitoring stations, 24 recorded "moderate" air, 31 "poor" and one "very poor" over the previous 24 hours.
stories.about: GRAP is the staged emergency plan for Delhi and its surrounding region: each stage adds restrictions as the air quality index crosses a threshold, and the CAQM, a central statutory body, decides when to impose or lift them.

sections.title: Cinema
sections.blurb: Ramayana nears Rs 1,500 crore worldwide, some Bond fans object to Robert Pattinson, Avengers: Doomsday passes Rs 10 crore in advance sales in India, and Cliff Booth draws warm first reactions.

stories.title: Ramayana Part 1 reaches Rs 821 crore net in India after 13 days and stands just short of Rs 1,500 crore worldwide.
stories.summary: Sacnilk estimates the film took Rs 32.00 crore net on Monday 16 November and Rs 28.70 crore on Tuesday 17 November, for Rs 821.30 crore India net and Rs 1,483.50 crore worldwide gross. Director Ram Gopal Varma called it the "Taj Mahal of Indian cinema" in a post on X on 17 November.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available (the Reddit file was empty at writing time) · Sacnilk, The Week, India TV News, Free Press Journal, NewsBytes · velocity: high, daily figures still drive headlines and the Rs 1,500 crore mark is expected on day 14
detail: What is new since the 16 November edition (which carried the day 11 total of Rs 760.60 crore India net): the first two weekdays of the second week. Sacnilk estimates Rs 32.00 crore India net on day 12 (Monday 16 November) and Rs 28.70 crore on day 13 (Tuesday 17 November), a fall of 10.3% from Monday. The 13-day India total is Rs 821.30 crore net and Rs 981.50 crore gross.

Sacnilk puts overseas gross at Rs 502.00 crore (Rs 12.00 crore of it on day 13) and the worldwide gross at Rs 1,483.50 crore. The Week, citing Sacnilk, wrote that the film is expected to pass Rs 1,500 crore worldwide on day 14 (Wednesday 18 November). Sacnilk notes that its figures are estimates and can differ from the producers' numbers.

By language on day 13, Sacnilk gives Hindi Rs 21.00 crore from 17,867 shows, Malayalam Rs 2.35 crore, Kannada Rs 2.10 crore, Tamil Rs 1.75 crore and Telugu Rs 1.50 crore. Overall occupancy was 22.9%, against 47.9% on the second Sunday. Monday's Rs 32.00 crore was the film's lowest day until Tuesday went below it.

On 17 November the director Ram Gopal Varma wrote on X: "The Ramayana will eventually remain as the Taj Mahal of Indian cinema" and "Nobody now cares about how much it cost to build the Taj Mahal", a reply to the debate over the film's cost, as reported by the Free Press Journal. The Week gives the budget as Rs 4,000 crore for the two parts together. Varma also praised Yash's Ravana as a performance "of many decades".
The Week adds that Ramayana is the fastest Hindi film to reach Rs 300 crore in South India. Part 2 is planned for 2028.

stories.title: Some James Bond fans complain that Robert Pattinson is "not alpha male", and Puck reports that Josh O'Connor was the director's first choice.
stories.summary: The Hollywood Reporter collected fan complaints about the new 007 on 16 November and noted that most reactions were positive. On 17 November outlets citing Matt Belloni's Puck newsletter reported that Josh O'Connor had been Denis Villeneuve's early favourite and withdrew.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · The Hollywood Reporter (syndicated on Yahoo), CBR, The Playlist, World of Reel, Yahoo UK, many aggregators · velocity: high, second and third day of reaction to the 16 November casting
detail: What is new since the 16 November edition (which carried Amazon MGM's confirmation of Pattinson as the seventh Bond): the reaction, and a report on how the casting was decided.

The Hollywood Reporter's James Hibberd wrote on 16 November that fans were already complaining in the Daily Mail comment section, under Amazon MGM's Instagram post, on X and on Reddit. The repeated complaints: that Pattinson lacks charm and swagger and is not an "alpha male" or action type (one commenter wrote "I've seen sexier potatoes"), that he is too closely tied to Batman ("You can't have the same actor playing Batman and James Bond at the same time"), and that he would suit a Bond villain better.

The same article says that plenty of reactions, if not most, were positive, and that the pattern is old: Daniel Craig was called not handsome enough in 2005. The sample is a set of online comments, not a poll.

On 17 November The Playlist, World of Reel and others relayed a Puck newsletter item by Matt Belloni: Josh O'Connor was Denis Villeneuve's early favourite, "so much so that several insiders believed the gig was his to lose", but he had reservations about the baggage of the role, went in and out of testing and then took himself out of the running. Belloni also described the closing of Pattinson's deal as arduous.
The O'Connor account rests on one newsletter. Neither O'Connor, Villeneuve nor Amazon MGM has confirmed it.

stories.title: Avengers: Doomsday passes Rs 10 crore in opening-day advance sales in India within about 19 hours, a month before release.
stories.summary: Sacnilk reported on 17 November that about 1 lakh tickets were sold at PVR, INOX and Cinepolis in roughly 19 hours. Bollywood Hungama reported a Rs 4,300 ticket for a midnight 4DX show in Navi Mumbai, which it calls the most expensive film ticket sold in India.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Sacnilk, Bollywood Hungama, DNA, NewsBytes · velocity: high, booking opened at midnight on 17 November and figures rose through the day
detail: What is new since the 16 November edition (which carried the plan to open presales): bookings opened at midnight on Tuesday 17 November, and the first numbers are in. The film releases in India on Thursday 17 December, one day before the United States.

DNA, citing Sacnilk, reported more than 50,000 tickets and over Rs 3 crore in the first hours, with BookMyShow selling about 8,000 tickets an hour. By 9:47 PM IST Sacnilk reported that the opening-day advance had passed Rs 10 crore gross, with about 1 lakh tickets sold at the three national chains (PVR, INOX, Cinepolis) in roughly 19 hours.

For comparison, Sacnilk gives first-24-hour advance gross at the same three chains as Rs 8.27 crore for Avengers: Endgame (2019), Rs 6.56 crore for Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021) and Rs 5.02 crore for Avengers: Infinity War (2018). It adds a caution: those films opened booking much closer to release, and Endgame sold over 1 million BookMyShow tickets in its first 24 hours, a figure Doomsday has not reached.

Bollywood Hungama reported that Cinepolis Seawoods in Navi Mumbai priced a ticket for the 12:01 am 4DX show on 17 December at Rs 4,300, the first single ticket above Rs 4,000 in India; the previous high it cites is Rs 3,170 for Ramayana at PVR Lower Parel. The film has no IMAX release in India because Dune: Part Three opens the same week and holds those screens.
DNA says early trade projections put the opening day at Rs 90 to 100 crore net. These are projections, not results.

stories.title: First reactions to David Fincher's Cliff Booth film are mostly warm, and Brad Pitt says a Leonardo DiCaprio cameo was dropped because of the prosthetics it needed.
stories.summary: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth premiered in Los Angeles on 16 November; The Hollywood Reporter collected reactions that call it a "pure riot", with a few mixed voices. Pitt told the same outlet that bringing back DiCaprio's Rick Dalton "just seemed like a big ask".
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · The Hollywood Reporter, Variety, NME, Screen Rant, Yahoo · velocity: medium to high, reviews are embargoed until 19 November and the film opens on 25 November
stories.about: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is a sequel to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood (2019), written by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher, with Brad Pitt again as stuntman Cliff Booth.
detail: The film had its premiere in Los Angeles on Monday 16 November. Social-media reactions were allowed; full reviews are embargoed until 19 November, The Hollywood Reporter wrote.

The reactions it collected were mostly positive: Variety's Clayton Davis called it "a wild, hilarious hangout movie", Courtney Howard called it "a pure riot", and Germain Lussier wrote that it "is my favorite movie of the year and it's not even close". Two were cooler: Erik Anderson of AwardsWatch found it "tonally a bit messy", and Todd Gilchrist wrote that he is "not yet convinced" that Tarantino's writing and Fincher's precision fit together.

At the premiere Pitt explained to The Hollywood Reporter why Leonardo DiCaprio does not appear as Rick Dalton. The sequel is set eight years later and its trailer says Rick "got too fat", so a cameo would have needed heavy prosthetics and, by Screen Rant's account, about two weeks of preparation. "It was talked about for a while, but it just seemed like a big ask," Pitt said. The film has a couple of tributes to Rick instead.

The cast includes Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Peter Weller, Timothy Olyphant and Yahya Abdul-Mateen II. It opens in IMAX cinemas only on 25 November and arrives on Netflix on 23 December.

sources.name: The Hollywood Reporter via Yahoo (first reactions)

stories.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is tracked for an opening of $80 million or more in North America this weekend.
stories.summary: Deadline reports that the film's presales are Lionsgate's best since the pandemic and puts the opening at $80 to $100 million. On Monday 16 November the current leader Ebenezer took $1.36 million, for $20.4 million in four days, according to The Numbers.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Deadline, The Numbers, Koimoi, Rotten Tomatoes, tracking blogs · velocity: high, early IMAX shows start 18 November and the wide release is 20 November
detail: What is new since the 16 November edition (which carried Ebenezer's $19.0 million opening as an estimate): Monday figures and the preview of the 20 November weekend.

The Numbers' daily chart for Monday 16 November has Ebenezer first with $1,363,033, for a four-day total of $20,375,050 in 3,535 cinemas. That total implies a three-day weekend of about $19.0 million, in line with Sunday's estimate. Godzilla Minus Zero took $666,000 on Monday for $49.7 million in 11 days.

The fifth Hunger Games film opens wide on Friday 20 November, with early IMAX and premium screenings from Wednesday 18 November. Deadline reported that its presales are the best for Lionsgate since the pandemic, ahead of Michael and of Wicked at the same point, and raised the opening forecast to a floor of $80 million, up from $60 to $70 million. Other trackers go higher: Box Office Theory projects $105 to $140 million.

The previous film in the series, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes (2023), opened to $44.6 million, the lowest of the franchise; the two Mockingjay films opened to about $122 million and $103 million. Francis Lawrence directs, Joseph Zada plays the young Haymitch, and the reported budget is $170 to $200 million. No other wide release opens against it; Disney's Hexed and the Cliff Booth film follow on 25 November.
Tracking is a forecast. Deadline notes that films with a young female audience can be front-loaded.

stories.title: Britain's Ministry of Justice investigates whether Russell Brand broke prison rules with a message, read out by his wife, in which he says he is not guilty.
stories.summary: Brand was jailed for 10 and a half years on 9 November for one rape and three sexual assaults. Downing Street called the message, broadcast on his YouTube channel on 15 November, "clearly appalling", as reported by The Guardian and relayed by CBC, The Hill and Yahoo.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · The Guardian (original report), CBC, The Hill, TMZ, The Hollywood Reporter, Parade · velocity: medium, government reaction on 16 and 17 November
detail: Russell Brand, 51, the comedian and actor (Forgetting Sarah Marshall, Get Him to the Greek), was convicted at Southwark Crown Court of one count of rape and three of sexual assault, offences involving four women, and sentenced on 9 November to 10 and a half years.

On 15 November his wife read notes from him on the couple's YouTube programme. They included the line "As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for" and described his move from Wandsworth prison to HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire.

The Guardian first reported that the Ministry of Justice is investigating. Prisoners may say they are innocent, but they are banned from statements that distress victims, and passing remarks to family for publication can bring loss of privileges or extra days. A Downing Street spokesperson called the message "clearly appalling"; Justice Secretary Alex Norris called the broadcast "completely unacceptable". Prison sources told The Guardian the notes may have been written before the conviction.

London's Victims' Commissioner said the claim will "certainly retraumatise his victims". A woman who was among six who made allegations in the 2023 investigation by The Times, The Sunday Times and Channel 4 (none of the six was a complainant in the trial) called the message "appalling"; Brand denies her allegation. The Metropolitan Police said after the verdict that an investigation into rape allegations by two further women continues.

stories.title: Ali Fazal leads a five-part BBC and CBC adaptation of A Passage to India, written and directed by Richie Mehta.
stories.summary: Deadline and Variety reported on 17 November that Fazal plays Dr Aziz, with Fiona Shaw as Mrs Moore, Tom Mison as Fielding and Naseeruddin Shah as Godbole. The series is filming in India; no air date is set.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Deadline, Variety, Bollywood Hungama, T2 Online, NewsBytes · velocity: medium, a one-day casting announcement
stories.about: Richie Mehta is the Canadian writer and director of Delhi Crime, which won an International Emmy. A Passage to India is E.M. Forster's 1924 novel about British rule in India, last filmed by David Lean in 1984.
detail: This is a television series, carried here because of its cast. Ali Fazal (Mirzapur, Victoria and Abdul) plays Dr Aziz, the Indian doctor accused of assaulting an Englishwoman. Tom Mison plays Fielding, Fiona Shaw plays Mrs Moore, Gwilym Lee her son Ronny, and Clare Hughes plays Adela. Naseeruddin Shah plays Godbole, Shahana Goswami plays Amrit Rao and Danish Husain plays Hamidullah, Bollywood Hungama reported.

It is an official UK and Canada co-production by Parti Productions, Working Title Television and Mehta's company, commissioned by the BBC and CBC, for BBC One, BBC iPlayer, CBC TV and CBC Gem. NBCUniversal Global TV Distribution sells it elsewhere. Filming is under way in India.

stories.title: The Tamil film OM: Chapter 1, with Dhanush and Mammootty, opens on Friday 20 November and Koimoi forecasts a first day above Rs 15 crore net in India.
stories.summary: Koimoi expects the action thriller to open at Rs 15 crore or more, which could be the best opening for either star. Sacnilk reported only limited advance booking by the afternoon of 17 November, before wider sales opened.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Koimoi (two forecasts), Sacnilk, Filmibeat · velocity: medium, rising into release week
stories.about: OM: Chapter 1 (Udhiram, The Blood Wood) is a Tamil action thriller directed by Rajkumar Periasamy, who made Amaran, and produced by Dhanush's Wunderbar Films with RTake Studios.
detail: The film is the main Indian release of 20 November and has no large rival that day. Koimoi forecasts Rs 15 crore or more net in India on day one. It says that would put the film near Dhanush's best opening (Rs 15.81 crore for Tere Ishk Mein) and among the top five Tamil openers of 2026 (Karuppu opened at Rs 15.5 crore), and would be Mammootty's best start, above the Rs 9.8 crore of Patriot. Koimoi cites reports of a Rs 200 crore budget.

Sacnilk's snapshot at 4 PM IST on 17 November showed only Rs 19.83 lakh in advance sales including blocked seats, from 92 shows in a few cities; wider booking was due to open at 5 PM that day, so the figure says little yet. Sacnilk also reports that PEN Marudhar holds the North India theatrical rights. Sai Pallavi is in the cast, Filmibeat reported, and the music is by Sai Abhyankkar. The Koimoi pages could not be fetched (blocked); their figures are taken from search results.

stories.title: Distributors are reported to be offering more than Rs 100 crore for the all-India rights to Golmaal 5.
stories.summary: Bollywood Hungama, citing one unnamed trade source, reported on 17 November a bidding war for the Rohit Shetty comedy with Ajay Devgn and Akshay Kumar, which releases on 8 January 2027.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Bollywood Hungama exclusive only · velocity: low to medium, one trade report
detail: Bollywood Hungama's source says several distributors are ready to pay over Rs 100 crore for the all-India theatrical rights, and that overseas distributors have made offers on a similar scale. No bidder is named. The decision lies with Rohit Shetty, Authum Studios and Katha Entertainment Studios, who are said to prefer a distributor that takes a lower commission and can deliver a wide release.

The cast is Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Shreyas Talpade, Tusshar Kapoor and Akshay Kumar, with Sharman Joshi back for the first time since the 2006 original. The last film, Golmaal Again (2017), took Rs 205.69 crore in India by Bollywood Hungama's count. Golmaal 5 is dated 8 January 2027, the first sequel in the series not to open at Diwali. The report rests on one anonymous source.

stories.title: Salman Khan is reported to have begun a 10-day shoot in Pune for a film with Nayanthara, said to be titled Monster.
stories.summary: Pinkvilla, citing an unnamed source and relayed by Bollywood Hungama on 17 November, says the schedule began on 15 November and that a teaser is being considered for Khan's birthday on 27 December. The makers have confirmed neither the title nor the date.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Pinkvilla (original), Filmfare (title), Bollywood Hungama · velocity: low, a production update
detail: The film is directed by Vamshi Paidipally (Maharshi, Varisu) and presented by Dil Raju's Sri Venkateswara Creations, for release in Hindi, Telugu and Tamil. It is the first film to pair Salman Khan with Nayanthara. Seema Biswas is reported to be part of the Pune schedule, in which dramatic scenes are being shot.
The title Monster comes from Filmfare and has not been announced. The report says the team is aiming for a cinema release at Eid 2027. All of this comes from one unnamed source.
